newsitem.title: CANADA: IPL mulling oil line to BP refinery.
newsitem.headline: IPL mulling oil line to BP refinery.

text.p: IPL Energy Inc unit Interprovincial Pipe Line Inc expects to learn by the end of this quarter whether it will build a 150,000 barrel per day crude oil pipeline in the U.S. Midwest, Interprovincial president and chief executive Pat Daniel said on Monday.
Daniel said the pipeline would extend from the company's Lakehead system east of Chicago to BP's refinery in Toledo, Ohio.

"We have talked with BP and they're currently determining whether they are prepared to make the investment in their refinery to add the Canadian heavy crude...coking capacity," Daniel said following a speech to an oil conference.
"We expect to hear from them toward the end of the first quarter as to whether they are prepared to go ahead."
He said BP had indicated during recent regulatory hearings that the company favored adding the new capacity for processing heavy crude.

The move would follow a similar deal between IPL and Mobil Corp announced last year in which IPL, which operates the main crude oil pipeline system to the U.S. from Canada, took a stake in Mobil's Mustang pipeline to Patoka, Ill. from Chicago offering extended access for Canadian oil producers.
Daniel said he believed several Midwest refiners would be motivated over the next 10 years to add coking capacity rather than staking their feedstock requirements on offshore supplies.

Production of Canadian heavy oil is forecast to grow by leaps and bounds over the next decade as new heavy oil and oil sands projects in the Athabasca region of Alberta are completed and brought on stream.

"I think the refiners can look upstream and realize that that this isn't a short-term blip -- It's a long-term, secure supply of heavy. They obviously have to look at their forecasts for the light and heavy differential and feel confident that heavy crude is going to be favorably priced," he said.
